title: Entitlement Forensics, Evidence Retention, and SDLC Integration Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook defines the operational procedures to capture, preserve, and retain entitlement and authorization evidence across Redwood Inference services. It combines RBAC snapshotting, audit log correlation, forensic collection practices, SDLC gate integration, and long-term evidence packaging so teams can produce audit-ready bundles for legal, compliance, and incident investigations.

Scope: Applies to: authz-service, identity-broker, audit-pipeline, evidence-orchestrator, model-serving control plane, and all customer tenancy metadata. Does NOT cover application-level PII redaction (see data-residency-and-retention policy).

Owners and collaborators
- Primary owner: Security Engineering (security@redwood.example.com)
- Secondary owners: SRE (logging pipeline), Platform (deployment control plane), Legal (evidence retention approvals)
- Escalation: Head of Security -> Chief Compliance Officer -> Legal Counsel

Definitions
- Entitlement snapshot: a point-in-time export of role bindings, principal-to-role mappings, and attribute assertions for a tenant/resource.
- Evidence bundle: a tamper-evident package containing relevant logs, snapshots, artifacts, checksums, and a manifest.

Quick summary of responsibilities
- RBAC snapshotting: Security Engineering (daily incremental, weekly full)
- Audit log collection: SRE / Audit Pipeline (real-time ingestion; 99.9% delivery SLA)
- Evidence packaging & handoff: Evidence Orchestration team (policy enforcement)
- Retention policy enforcement: Legal + Security (approval for retention > standard)

SLOs and thresholds
- Audit delivery SLA: 99.9% of auth and decision events ingested into audit-pipeline within 10s.
- Snapshot freshness: daily incremental snapshots within 6 hours of UTC midnight; full weekly snapshot retained for 26 months.
- Evidence integrity: every evidence bundle must include SHA256 checksums for each file and a signed manifest.
- Missing-log alert: Pager duty if missing >1% of expected decision events in a 1-hour window or if sampling shows gaps larger than 30s for service-critical endpoints.

Retention matrix (canonical)
| Artifact type | Minimum retention | Storage tier | Notes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| AuthZ decision logs (per-request) | 2 years | Hot -> cold | Hot for 90 days, then cold; longer for regulated tenants on request |
| Entitlement snapshots (full) | 26 months | Cold | Weekly full snapshots + daily incrementals for 90 days |
| Evidence bundles (incident) | 7 years | Cold or legal vault | Legal-reviewed retention longer on litigation |
| Audit pipeline raw events (compressed) | 24 months | Cold | Access restricted; index preserved for 6 months |
| SDLC approval artifacts (rbac-scan results) | 3 years | Hot | Tied to release artifacts and CVE fixes |

RBAC snapshotting procedure (runbook)
1. Trigger: automated job 'rbac-snapshot-agent' runs daily at 02:00 UTC; full snapshot runs Sunday 03:00 UTC.
2. Data collected:
   - role-bindings.yaml (k8s style roleBindings for control-plane resources)
   - attribute-assertions.json (ABAC attributes for dynamic entitlements)
   - service-account-to-key-metadata.csv
3. Commands (examples)
   - Control plane (K8s): kubectl get rolebinding --all-namespaces -o yaml > role-bindings-$(date +%F).yaml
   - Authz API export: curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXPORT_TOKEN" https://authz.redwood/internal/v1/export?since=YYYY-MM-DD > entitlement-export.json
4. Validation: rbac-snapshot-verify role-bindings-....yaml -> outputs SHA256 and compares against last incremental. If verification fails, create P0 ticket and pause automatic deletion.
5. Storage: snapshots are added to evidence-store, indexed by collection_id and tenant_id, and immutably archived with at-rest encryption (KMS key: projects/redwood/evidence).

Audit log correlation and evidence assembly
- Objective: For any investigation, produce a correlated view of: (a) entitlement state, (b) authz decisions, (c) actor identity flows, (d) service-level telemetry (latency, errors).
- Correlation keys: event.request_id, tenant_id, principal_id, model_request_id.
- Assembly steps:
  1. Identify incident window (start/end timestamps).
  2. Pull audit events from audit-pipeline for window using event.request_id prefix 
     - API: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_Q" "https://audit.redwood.internal/query?start=...&end=...&tenant=..." > events.ndjson
  3. Retrieve entitlement snapshots covering start time (choose full or incremental that contains start)
  4. Run correlation script: evidence-orchestrator correlate --events events.ndjson --snapshots snapshot.tar.gz --out bundle-<id>
  5. Generate manifest with SHA256 sums and sign with evidence-signing-key (kms-sign).

Evidence bundle schema (manifest fields)
- bundle_id: string
- incident_window: ISO timestamps
- included_snapshots: list of snapshot filenames
- included_logs: list of log files with ranges
- checksums: map filename->sha256 (stored in manifest)
- signer: service principal that produced the bundle
- legal_approval: reference id if retention is beyond default

Legal & data-residency controls
- Tenant residency: evidence bundles for tenant data submitted to any region must respect tenant residency policies. If evidence crosses jurisdictional boundaries, Legal must approve cross-border transfer before longer-term retention.
- PII handling: apply automated redaction pipeline for fields flagged in data-classification (PII, PHI). Redaction is logged and included as a transformation step in the manifest.

SDLC integration (release and predeploy gates)
- Requirement: Every release pipeline must run 'rbac-scan' and 'authorization-integration-test' before canary rollout.
- Gate criteria:
  1. rbac-scan exit code 0 (no high severity entitlement drift)
  2. authorization-integration-test: >=99.95% deterministic decision parity with baseline for 1,000 sampled decision traces
  3. Evidence traceability: release artifact must include snapshot-id tag used to generate runtime entitlements for that release (release metadata key: runtime_entitlement_snapshot).
- CI jobs to add to templates: rbac-scan, entitlement-diff, evidence-manifest-generator. Example GitHub Actions step:
  - name: Run RBAC scan
    run: ./ci/rbac-scan --out rbac-results.json

Incident response (security) — forensic checklist
1. Triage: capture incident metadata, affected tenants, suspected time window, attack vector (if known).
2. Containment: if a compromised principal is identified, rotate credentials and disable sessions via identity-broker immediately; create temporary role locks.
3. Evidence collection: follow Audit log correlation steps above. Clone evidence to an isolated forensic bucket (forensics-<incident-id>) with IAM restricted to Security+Legal.
4. Chain of custody: Every handoff of the bundle must be recorded in the manifest with user, timestamp, and purpose. Use evidence-orchestrator handoff --to legal --record.
5. Analysis: security engineers run offline analysis; SRE provides resource-level telemetry; Legal evaluates regulatory obligations.
6. Post-incident retention decision: by default, evidence bundles are retained 7 years; if legal opens a case, preservation holds are applied and extended per Legal direction.

Risk and exception process (short form)
- Low-risk exceptions (short-lived dev experiments): request via access-exceptions form; auto-expire after 72 hours; Security approves with 24h SLA.
- Medium-risk exceptions (multi-team, up to 30 days): documented risk acceptance, evidence of compensating controls, quarterly review.
- High-risk exceptions ( >30 days or production-wide): Must go to Security Risk Committee and receive written approval with mitigation plan.
- Exception template (required fields): owner, scope, start/end, compensating controls, rollback criteria, monitoring metrics.

Monitoring and automated controls
- RBAC drift detection: daily job compares desired state (git-controlled entitlement manifests) vs snapshot; alert if >5% of principals changed unexpectedly.
- Audit pipeline health: Prometheus metrics (audit_ingest_latency_seconds, audit_ingest_error_rate) with alerts:
  - P1 if 5m error_rate > 0.5%
  - P2 if 1h latency p95 > 30s
- Evidence signing failures: immediate P0 paged to security-oncall.

Templates and checklists (appendix)
- Evidence bundle checklist:
  1. Included manifest with signer and checksums
  2. Entitlement snapshots used and timestamped
  3. Audit logs for incident window (raw and parsed)
  4. Service telemetry (traces/metrics relevant to incident)
  5. Redaction summary (fields transformed)
  6. Chain-of-custody log with user actions

- RBAC exception template (example)
  - owner: team-x
  - scope: service=authz-service, env=prod
  - period: 2026-01-01 -> 2026-02-01
  - compensating controls: 2FA required, periodic manual review weekly
  - rollback criteria: any anomalous decision-rate increase > 3x baseline

Appendix: common CLI snippets
- Snapshot export (authz):
  AUDIT_TOKEN=$(vault read -field=token secret/audit/export)
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_TOKEN" "https://authz.redwood/internal/v1/export?full=true" | gzip > snapshot-$(date +%F).json.gz
  sha256sum snapshot-$(date +%F).json.gz > snapshot-$(date +%F).sha256

- Evidence bundle creation (example):
  evidence-orchestrator assemble --events events.ndjson --snapshots snapshot.tar.gz --out /forensics/bundle-<id>.tar.gz
  kms sign --key projects/redwood/keys/evidence --in /forensics/bundle-<id>.manifest.json --out /forensics/bundle-<id>.manifest.sig

- Demo query for audit events:
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $AUDIT_Q" "https://audit.redwood.internal/query?tenant=tenant-123&from=2026-02-10T00:00:00Z&to=2026-02-10T01:00:00Z" | jq -c .

Related pages and required reading

End of playbook
